items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: In other words, Charlie took the other thing, -- Barnet -- and did an actual copy of Duke's music

ctx.x: That's right. My earliest influences came back and Ralph was very heavily influenced by Sweetpea and by Duke and so we were all shooting for the same thing. We didn't want to be like Duke, but we sure wanted to sound good like him.

In other words, Charlie took the other thing, -- Barnet -- and did an actual copy of Duke's music, and that to me would have been very distasteful, and that would be dishonoring a great man and a great group of musicians. But what we did was try to capture the feeling, warmth and enthu-
siasm, and if we could outswing him, then we'd figure we'd won the game.

items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Oh, June Hutton. And Woody Herman. So, you know, it was an interesting stable. I mean they're all people that you could be proud to say, "I represent them."

ctx.x: Oh, Peggy Lee. We had Mel Torme. We had Nat Cole. We had Nellie Lutcher. We had Rafael Mendez. We had -- oh, let's see, there's something I'm forgetting there. Oh, June Hutton. And Woody Herman. So, you know, it was an interesting stable. I mean they're all people that you could be proud to say, "I represent them."
